editorial: If you grew up hearing Robbie Williams on the radio, this movie will hit you right in the feelings. Better Man tells the story of the British pop star's wild ride from a small-town kid to the youngest member of Take That, and then into his solo career. The big twist is that Robbie is played as a CGI monkey the whole time, which sounds weird but actually works. It makes his struggles with fame, addiction, and self-doubt feel fresh and surprisingly moving. The music is fantastic, with big concert scenes that feel alive and loud. The supporting cast is strong, especially the actors playing his bandmates and family. The pacing keeps things moving, though the middle drags a bit during the darker moments. The monkey gimmick never gets old, and the emotional beats land hard. It is a bold, strange, and heartfelt biopic that takes real risks. You will laugh, cringe, and maybe tear up.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Robbie performs a massive solo concert while battling his inner demons, shown as the monkey version of himself fighting through crowds of critics and past mistakes. He reconciles with his father, who finally shows up to support him. The movie ends with Robbie accepting himself, monkey and all, and stepping into the spotlight with confidence. It is a hopeful, emotional finish that ties his whole journey together.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music biopics, pop culture, or bold storytelling.
